name: Đilasism
summary: Đilasism is the democratic-socialist dissent of Milovan Đilas, a Yugoslav Partisan leader who broke with Tito. It holds that communist party-states create a privileged bureaucratic new class, rejects one-party monopoly and enforced ideology, and calls for a legal democratic socialist opposition, free expression and the separation of party from state.
scope: The Đilas of 1950 to 1995: the Borba articles and 1954 break, The New Class (1957), and his later dissident writing and opposition to Yugoslavia's breakup. Excludes the pre-1953 Đilas as Stalinist and Titoist hardliner and the loose pejorative use of the term. The sources opened give a few core positions in detail; most other statements are inferred. Only the first part of The New Class was read, in Swedish.

sources.title: Milovan Djilas (obituary tribute)
sources.author: Tribune
sources.usedFor: Contemporary tribute: his insistence that denying democracy poisons socialism.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: He attacked bureaucratic control of the economy but remained a socialist; sources give no endorsement of free markets as better than governments.

public-ownership.rationale: He argued that nominal collective ownership is camouflage for bureaucratic ownership, so state ownership alone is not the answer; adherents are split on the form it should take.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Corporations are not his subject; his target was the party-state's economic monopoly.

cut-welfare.rationale: Never addressed; democratic socialism opposes cutting welfare.

worker-ownership.rationale: In 1950 he helped formulate workers' self-management, in which workers run enterprises, though he later criticised its bureaucratic implementation.

strong-leader.rationale: He condemned the concentration of power in a party and its leader as the root of communist despotism, and broke with Tito over it.

state-harmful.rationale: He wanted the state and party separated and the state to wither as Marxists hoped, but he did not call it unnecessary and harmful now.

empower-police-military.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.

reviewHistory.rationale: He criticised the secret police and party control of coercive forces; more authority for them runs against his stance.
reviewHistory.author: claude-sonnet-5-5

reviewHistory.rationale: Moved (statement review, 2026-11-11) to police-more-powers: its rationale is about police powers, and this statement now asks only about military spending.
reviewHistory.author: claude-opus-5-5

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Sex work was never a topic for him in the sources read, and democratic socialists divide on it.

traditional-family.rationale: Family structure is absent from his political writing as summarised; no inference is safe.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Gender theory is absent from everything read about him.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Mixed: he valued Montenegrin and Serbian literary culture but opposed nationalism; sources give no clear position.

gradual-change.rationale: He accepted that only if the new class gave up its monopolies could change begin, favouring reform of the system over revolution.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Only evidence is his backing of UN condemnation of Soviet action in Hungary, too thin to place a view on strengthening the UN.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He objected to Soviet intervention but left no view on humanitarian war.

open-borders.rationale: Borders as a theme are absent from the sources; neutral.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Technology as a theme is not in his political writing as summarised.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Energy policy is absent from the sources read.

revolution-justified.rationale: He had led a revolution himself and accepted its role in Russia, China and Yugoslavia, but argued that communist revolutions end in despotism; adherents split.

central-planning.rationale: He described the centralised party-state economy as serving a bureaucratic class and left early on to advocate decentralisation.

basic-income.rationale: No evidence he considered unconditional income schemes.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Not a stated aim; he disavowed original Marxist utopian predictions.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No evidence of anti-banking views; as a socialist reformer he would not leave money to the market.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies fixing wages and prices resemble the party-controlled organisations he criticised, though he never addressed corporatism.

one-party-rule.rationale: He wrote that communist single-party monopoly of power, property and ideology is the system's core evil and called in 1954 for a second democratic socialist party.

democracy-best.rationale: The Tribune tribute credits him with insisting that denying democracy poisons socialism; he moved to democratic socialist ideas.

workers-councils.rationale: He helped devise workers' self-management in 1950, but his later democratic socialism rested on party pluralism rather than councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: He opposed Yugoslavia's breakup, proposing only a loose confederation, so he would not endorse a general right to secede.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: A secular socialist who denounced ideological orthodoxy of all kinds; scripture-based law is far from his stance.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Never discussed; privatised justice and defence contradict any socialist outlook.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He opposed 1990s ethnic nationalism and the dissolution of multiethnic Yugoslavia.

class-struggle-history.rationale: He retained Marxist class analysis, naming a new exploiting class, but said Marx's concrete predictions failed.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous rights are outside his documented concerns.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations never come up in what I read.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Socialist moral outlook points against celebrating self-interest, though he never addressed the claim.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He criticised the communist system for securing no individual rights; the Tribune notes his insistence on democracy.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Environmental philosophy is absent from the sources read.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He accepted industrialisation as the setting of communist revolutions and never rejected it.

results-over-ideology.rationale: His critique is that ideology became dogma; he disliked orthodoxy, but judged by principle too.

means-match-ends.rationale: Central to his argument that revolution's despotic means produced a despotic outcome.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He retained the ideals of equality and brotherhood but doubted communist utopian promises.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He argued exploitation now lies in the bureaucracy's control of surplus, not private profit alone.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He wrote that Lenin's hopes for a free classless society via dictatorship failed and led to despotism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: His writing targets communist states; the sources do not give his view on capitalism and imperialism.

individual-rights-only.rationale: He wanted individual rights secured but sources give no view on group rights.

conscription.rationale: Military service policy is absent from the sources read.

total-state.rationale: He described the communist state as directing every sphere, demanding uniformity in political, philosophical and moral views, and condemned it.

national-rebirth.rationale: He opposed the radical nationalism of the 1990s Yugoslav breakup.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He opposed the nationalist wars of Yugoslavia's breakup.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Rule by personal loyalty is the reverse of the legal, democratic order he sought.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom-like obligations contradict every part of his thought on equality and workers' freedom.

single-common-good.rationale: He criticised an ideology claiming a single correct line, preferring a plural democratic politics.

workplace-democracy.rationale: He co-formulated workers' self-management in 1950; democratic control of firms was a founding aim.

economic-freedom.rationale: He argued political freedom needs an end to the party's monopoly of property and power, but did not link it to market freedom as such.

rule-by-example.rationale: He attacked rulers' moral claims; law and plural politics preferred.

national-self-determination.rationale: He believed nations could seek independence from the Soviet Union but opposed Yugoslavia's dissolution; split.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He argued that in communist states the party-state itself served the new ruling class, extending the Marxist view of the state.

elite-replacement.rationale: Conspiratorial claims of this kind contradict his materialist analysis of elites.

proportional-representation.rationale: He backed multiparty democracy but not any electoral formula.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Gender structure analysis is absent from the sources.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: His central theme was that the party elite enjoys material privileges and monopoly while claiming to represent workers.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: He valued equality and brotherhood and demanded individual rights against party privilege.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He rejected Soviet domination, but sources do not give his view on whether socialism survives in one country.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: He held the state should separate from the party and wither, and he criticised the Stalinist justification for strengthening it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: The Tribune credits his belief that denial of democracy poisons socialism; democratic legitimacy follows.

population-transfer.rationale: He opposed the ethnic nationalism and violence of the 1990s Yugoslav wars.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He fought as a Partisan commander and later criticised violence; no absolute principle is documented.

separated-powers.rationale: He held party and state should be separated, and favoured pluralism and rule of law in place of party monopoly.

vanguard-party.rationale: He argued that the Leninist disciplined minority party turned into a ruling class of bureaucracy and centralised despotism.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: British housing policy is far from his concerns.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He defended multiethnic Yugoslavia against nationalist breakup.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He was imprisoned under such powers and opposed secret-police rule.

party-controls-media.rationale: Publications such as Beseda and Revija 57 were suppressed as Đilasist, and he fought ideological repression; he himself broke with party media control in 1954.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He urged looser party discipline after 1954.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: He was himself a writer persecuted for publications and opposed ideological censorship.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He argued communist industrialisation sacrificed freedom to a privileged class and that freedom, not just growth, was the aim.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Wikipedia's account of Đilasism says he held the Stalinist system to be inherently totalitarian, imperialist and state capitalist, and he later called its bureaucracy a new class.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: His support for Hungary in 1956 hints at sympathy for unconsented subjugation, but he gave no general view on annexation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: He opposed ideological uniformity, but the sources do not give a view on curbing churches.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He opposed breakup but also the 1990s wars; he suggested loose confederation, so force is not endorsed.

region-keeps-system.rationale: His confederation suggestion hints at autonomy but not on economic systems.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He condemned leader cults and the privileged class around the ruling party.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He argued that in communist states state power rests with party committees and secret police regardless of formal law, and condemned it.

leader-cult.rationale: He denounced the party leadership's privilege and single-leader rule in Yugoslavia.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He argued a new exploiting class emerges within socialism itself from party bureaucracy.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He opposed the nationalist territorial wars of the 1990s.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He opposed enforced ideological and moral uniformity.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He said Marx's concrete predictions proved wrong while keeping materialist class analysis; split.

moral-incentives.rationale: He pointed to the new class's material privileges as the reality behind socialist ideals.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: He noted communist revolutions were by small minorities, an approach he led in Yugoslavia and later condemned in effect.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He stressed that communist systems secure no individual rights; entrenched protections follow from his democratic turn.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He backed multiparty democracy but did not specify a constitutional model.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He persisted in political writing despite imprisonment.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: He says the new class relies on ideological uniformity and the secret police, not only consent.

party-own-road.rationale: Đilasism began as a breakaway from Titoism criticising the Soviet Union and Stalinism, and national paths to socialism are central to the Yugoslav deviation.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: A Partisan commander; anti-fascism was his wartime cause.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He called Yugoslavia totalitarian in 1954 and condemned communism as a failure.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He supported the Hungarian Revolution against Soviet intervention and objected to Yugoslavia's abstention on the UN vote, which led to his 1956 arrest.

non-intervention.rationale: He backed international condemnation of Soviet intervention in Hungary.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities are inconsistent with his analysis and his universalism.

informal-organisation.rationale: He advocated a legal opposition party, not informal groups.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He denounced Soviet domination of satellite states.

defeat-communism.rationale: He called communism a relic, but as a democratic socialist he favoured reform and engagement, not a campaign.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: He rejected communism and remained a democratic socialist, which is a third course.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He argued that communist rule excludes rival groups and called for opposition and a democratic socialist party.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He opposed enforced ideological and moral uniformity.

participatory-democracy.rationale: His 1950 self-management doctrine involved participation; later focus was party pluralism.

rich-first.rationale: He condemned privileged elites in communist systems.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: He criticised rule by party committees and secret police over formal law.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: He argued that concentrating property, understood as control, in one class endangers freedom; here the owners are the bureaucracy.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He opposed enforced ideological uniformity in philosophy and morals.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: He proposed a loose Yugoslav confederation but gave no explicit view on power-sharing.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: His critique is that the new class takes the largest share of workers' gains through control, not work.

independent-unions.rationale: He argued the party dominates all organisations in communist states; independence from party follows.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: He held that in communist states the working class is dominated by a bureaucracy, so the name socialism is hollow without it.

confederal-coordination.rationale: He suggested loose confederation for Yugoslavia but not city confederations.

person-over-state.rationale: He criticised communism for securing no individual rights; the individual should not be sacrificed.

smash-state-machine.rationale: His reform path is conditional on the new class yielding monopolies; smashing the state is a communist revolutionary idea he revised.

sacred-nation.rationale: He opposed nationalism that broke Yugoslavia.

workers-own-party.rationale: He called for a new democratic socialist party in 1954, but not specifically a workers' party.

defend-planned-state.rationale: He argued the planned party-state is a bureaucratic class system, so defending it as such is contrary.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Đilas condemned despotism and demanded legality, free expression and an end to the party's arbitrary power, which rules out killing suspects without trial.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He demanded a legal democratic socialist opposition party and called a single party's monopoly the core of the new class, so organised parties are necessary.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: He demanded an end to the party's monopoly over property, ideology and power and called for a second democratic socialist party.

police-more-powers.rationale: He criticised the secret police and party control of coercive forces; more authority for them runs against his stance. (Moved from empower-police-military, 2026-11-11, when that statement became about military spending alone.)

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Never addressed; democratic socialism opposes cutting welfare. (Carried over from cut-welfare, "Welfare programs create dependency and should be cut.", with the value reversed, 2026-11-11.)

missingStatements.text: A ruling party's officials form a privileged class that lives off the labour of the people they claim to represent.
missingStatements.rationale: The central thesis of The New Class is that the party bureaucracy of communist states is a new exploiting class through its control of property.

missingStatements.text: Public ownership of an economy is a disguise for control by a bureaucracy unless the public holds real democratic power.
missingStatements.rationale: Djilas called collective ownership camouflage for the political bureaucracy's real ownership.

missingStatements.text: A single party should not hold a monopoly over the state, the economy and ideology, even if it calls itself socialist.
missingStatements.rationale: He demanded an end to the new class's monopolies of property, ideology and power, and in 1954 called for a second democratic socialist party.

notes: Evidence is concentrated on one-party rule, party monopoly, revolution and the bureaucratic new class. Most other answers are low-confidence inferences, so the profile is likely to be thin on inclusion. His early self-management work and later pluralism differ in emphasis.
